clue.text: Spies trap lout with this bug

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so the spies enclose the lout

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency
a cad is a boorish, ill-mannered man

explanation.surface: An agent's surveillance team ensnares a yob using a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' looks like a hidden microphone in this spy story, but it is an insect; 'with this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a loud-singing insect of the order of true bugs, Hemiptera.

clue.text: Deco's stylised rules

indicators.note: rendered in a new style, so the letters of the word are given a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A remark about the design conventions of the Art Deco movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a set of rules, as in a highway code or code of conduct.

clue.text: Dismiss one on the register

definitions.meaning: to ... an officer is to discharge them from the armed forces in disgrace
a person who works at a till or cash register in a shop or bank

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for discharging an officer in disgrace and a noun for a till operator.

clue.text: Big waterfall isn't upriver by old city

parts.note: split 'upriver' into 'up' and 'river': what isn't up is down, and the river is the Po in northern Italy
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Directions to a great cascade that lies downstream beside an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upriver' has to be read as 'up' plus 'river'; 'by' just joins the pieces. Ur is the ancient Sumerian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is a heavy fall of rain, read here playfully as a great fall of water.

clue.text: Nice men upset by bearing superiority

indicators.note: knocked over and disordered, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Pleasant gentlemen are put out by someone's air of superiority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NICE MEN into EMINENC; 'by' is a link before E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is distinction or high rank, a state of standing above others.

clue.text: Many speak clearly, having reversed right to enrol

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

indicators.note: the letter named next is switched round with its neighbour, changing its place in the word

parts.note: to articulate is to pronounce words distinctly

explanation.surface: Lots of people talk distinctly, having changed their minds about the right to sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having reversed right' swaps the R with the T that follows it, so only those two letters change places; 'Many' is the Roman numeral at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To matriculate is to enrol formally at a university or college.

clue.text: Ordinary seaman or malcontent?

annotationWithheld.why: Ordinary seaman or malcontent? (6): the hidden letters sit in 'seamaN OR MALcontent', and the only indicator is 'content' inside 'malcontent', so that word is both fodder and indicator

clue.text: Not one Hibernian's initially up for the first one's feed

parts.note: no, as in 'no person', means not one

indicators.note: the first I (one) of the word is replaced by the letter named before 'for'

parts.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so a Hibernian is Irish

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: No Irishman was at first keen on the first course being served.
explanation.walkthrough: In IRISH, 'one' is I: 'initially up for the first one' puts U in place of its first I, giving URISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to feed, giving the food needed for growth.

clue.text: Wing's no longer taking the strain

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in that role
tension is strain, as in a pulled rope

explanation.surface: A bird's wing has stopped bearing the stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing's' is 'Wing is'; a wing here is an added part of a building, not a bird's limb. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is a wing added to a building, enlarging it.

clue.text: Deny losing is involved

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up inside, so is goes within the other word

parts.note: a team that is losing is down, as in two goals down

explanation.surface: Someone protests they had nothing to do with a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing is involved' looks like an anagram of LOSING IS, but there are too many letters; 'losing' is DOWN, with IS involved in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to deny any connection with, refuse to acknowledge.

clue.text: Dreamy romanticism is beginning to hold back the south of France

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: the start is the beginning

indicators.note: turns the following French word backwards

parts.note: sud is French for south

explanation.surface: A wistful mood begins to bring back memories of the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the French word round; 'is' and 'the' are links, and 'south of France' is French, not the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust, in a figurative sense, is a dreamy, romantic or magical quality.

clue.text: Second hint to include, if making it easy

indicators.note: the word for hint takes the other inside it

parts.note: an implication is something hinted at rather than said

explanation.surface: A tip for an exam: a quick suggestion including conditions makes the task easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is the abbreviation, not an ordinal; 'if' is fodder taken as written, not a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplification is the act of making something easier or plainer.

clue.text: What will come in race in the winds

indicators.note: to wind is to twist and turn, so these letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: Something bound to arrive during a race in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like a noun for gusts but is a verb, twisting IN RACE IN THE.
explanation.definitionFit: An inheritance is what will come to an heir on a death.

clue.text: Right to go in, even if striking elsewhere

indicators.note: the letter is to be placed inside the following word

parts.note: though means even if
workers who are striking are out

explanation.surface: Workers claim a right of entry even while a strike goes on at another site.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: throughout means everywhere, here read as in every other place too.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter stretches the sense: something happening all over is happening in other places as well as here.

clue.text: Shortened the line after reversion

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a row is a line
back means behind, as aft or after

explanation.surface: An editor trims a line of text after a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened the' gives TH, the article without its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A throwback is a reversion to an earlier type or ancestral trait.

clue.text: Sound match for easterner

indicators.note: the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A good partner for someone from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE said in British English sounds like THAI. A cup tie is a knockout football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a native of Thailand, in east Asia.

clue.text: Put moisture out through high point

parts.note: per means through or by, as in per post
a spire is a tall pointed steeple

explanation.surface: Getting moisture out by way of a tall tower.
explanation.definitionFit: To perspire is to sweat, giving out moisture through the skin.

clue.text: Brawl could precede the sack

definitions.meaning: put in front of the word sack it makes a backpack

explanation.definitionFit: A ruck is a rough scuffle, and the same word comes before sack to make rucksack.

clue.text: Set bed by lake

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Instructions to place a bed beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb but is a noun, a clique; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive set or circle of people.

clue.text: Prepare old fellow for final conflict?

parts.note: to arm is to make ready for battle
aged means old
a don is a fellow at a university

explanation.surface: Getting an elderly man ready for one last fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, at Oxford or Cambridge often a fellow of a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the biblical last battle between good and evil.

clue.text: Old order containing minute oriental rodents

indicators.note: one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: Doric is one of the classical orders of architecture
E, for east, means oriental

explanation.surface: An ancient decree that includes tiny Asian rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like 'tiny' but is M, and 'Old order' is an architectural order, not a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small, hibernating rodents.

clue.text: Sure to fail with a top that's round round round

indicators.note: goes round, so the first word encloses the next

parts.note: domed means having a rounded top
O is a round shape

explanation.surface: A spinning top going round and round is bound to fall over.
explanation.walkthrough: The three 'round's do three jobs: the first describes DOMED, the second is O, the third puts DOMED round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomed means certain to fail or come to grief.

clue.text: Immoderately lies like this for lime trees

parts.words: lies like this for lime trees
parts.note: the word 'lies' is what is left of 'lime trees' once a measure, a metre, is removed

explanation.surface: A lime grove is described as a place of untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking METRE out of LIME TREES leaves LIES, so 'lies' is 'lime trees' with no measure in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something without measure is to do it to excess, with no limit.

clue.text: Hit band

definitions.meaning: a band, as of leather round the waist

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning strike hard and a noun meaning strap or band.

clue.text: Herb that gets on in a dirty environment

indicators.note: the surroundings of something, so the other letters surround the next word

parts.note: grimy means dirty

explanation.surface: A plant that thrives in polluted soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that gets' and 'in' are links; 'environment' is the container signal, not ecology.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered herb of the rose family.

clue.text: To eat about 6 is excellent

indicators.note: goes about the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to dine is to eat
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Dining at about six is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, not 'roughly': six is the Roman numeral, held inside the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine is used informally to mean excellent or delightful.

clue.text: Castle guards want moat to be more than this!

definitions.text: moat to be more than this

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
need means want or lack

explanation.surface: Castle defenders insist that the moat should be deeper than this.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole idea that a moat should be deeper than this measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat only knee-height deep would be useless, so it must be deeper than that measure of water.

clue.text: Best man is had for the asking

indicators.note: is had means is contained, so the man is held inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
he is a man, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: The best man is available to anyone who requests him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best man' looks like the wedding role, but splits in two; 'is had' means held, and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or request, as in 'at the behest of'.
